summary: Prioritise water infrastructure, assess project financing and build decision-ready investment plans. Explore the five-day course and request details.
lede: Water infrastructure investment planning connects service needs and asset gaps with prioritised projects and funding options. Designed for water utility executives, planners and public investment and finance officials, the course covers service and asset assessment, lifecycle costing, economic appraisal and financing affordability. Participants compare project options, build Excel-based cash-flow and sensitivity scenarios, assess climate and delivery risks, and prepare an investment scorecard and decision brief.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape, appraise, finance or oversee water infrastructure investment decisions and need to link service priorities with credible funding plans.
modules: Water Assets and ISO 55000 Lifecycle Costs
Water Economic Appraisal and Cost-Benefit Analysis
Water Financing Options and PPP Appraisal
Water Investment Plans and Decision Reporting
prerequisites: Prior work in water-sector planning, infrastructure delivery, project appraisal or public finance is useful. You should be comfortable reviewing basic project costs and funding assumptions. No coding or programming is required; exercises use Excel-style financial analysis and structured case assumptions.
